questions.prompt: Describe the roles of the program counter (PC), memory address register (MAR) and current instruction register (CIR) during instruction fetching.
hints: Identify the key idea from CPU and fetch-decode-execute that the question is testing.
Use the wording of the question to decide which facts are relevant, then answer one mark point at a time.
questions.solution:
The PC stores the address of the next instruction. [B1]
The address is copied from the PC to the MAR. [B1]
The instruction at that memory address is fetched. [B1]
The fetched instruction is placed in the CIR ready to be decoded. [B1]

questions.prompt: Convert hexadecimal 7D to binary and denary.
hints: Identify the key idea from Binary and hexadecimal that the question is testing.
Work through the values in order and keep each intermediate step so you can check the final result.
questions.solution:
7 in hexadecimal is 0111 in binary. [B1]
D is 13, which is 1101 in binary. [B1]
So 7D = 01111101 in binary. [B1]
Its denary value is 7×16 + 13 = 125. [B1]

questions.prompt: Explain why adding 11110000 and 00110000 in an 8-bit unsigned register causes overflow.
hints: Identify the key idea from Binary arithmetic and overflow that the question is testing.
Link each point to why it matters or what effect it has, rather than only naming the term.
questions.solution:
11110000 is 240. [B1]

questions.solution:
11111111 represents 255. [B1]
Adding 1 gives 256. [B1]
256 requires a ninth bit. [B1]
The 8-bit result wraps to 00000000 and an overflow/carry condition occurs. [B1]

questions.solution:
